rules.title: OAuth code or refresh token reused

model.expr: sum by (what) (count_over_time({service="realm-server"} |= "boxel:oauth-provider" | json | drop __error__, __error_details__ | line_format `{{ if .log }}{{ regexReplaceAll "^\\[worker [^\\]]+\\]: " .log "" }}{{ else }}{{ regexReplaceAll "^\\[worker [^\\]]+\\]: " __line__ "" }}{{ end }}` | json | channel="boxel:oauth-provider" | event="reuse" [5m]))

annotations.title: {{ if $values }}[${ALERT_ENVIRONMENT}] An OAuth {{ .Labels.what }} was used twice{{ else }}[${ALERT_ENVIRONMENT}] DatasourceError: the OAuth rule "OAuth code or refresh token reused" could not run its query{{ end }}
annotations.summary: {{ if $values }}A spent authorization code, or a refresh token used outside its 30-second grace, came back to the token endpoint in the last 5 minutes. The provider ended its grant (reason reuse). Either the app mishandles its tokens, or someone copied one.{{ else }}Grafana could not run this rule's query. This is the rule's DatasourceError alert, and its Error annotation gives the reason. It shows nothing about OAuth activity. The query reads Loki: check the Loki task and its context canceled and context deadline exceeded errors.{{ end }}
annotations.runbook: The oauth-provider skill (Alerts), and the OAuth Provider dashboard.

rules.title: OAuth flows refused for their confirmation code

model.expr: sum by (network) (count_over_time({service="realm-server"} |= "boxel:oauth-provider" | json | drop __error__, __error_details__ | line_format `{{ if .log }}{{ regexReplaceAll "^\\[worker [^\\]]+\\]: " .log "" }}{{ else }}{{ regexReplaceAll "^\\[worker [^\\]]+\\]: " __line__ "" }}{{ end }}` | json | channel="boxel:oauth-provider" | event="authorization-refused" | reason="confirmation-code" [15m])) >= 5

annotations.title: {{ if $values }}[${ALERT_ENVIRONMENT}] Many OAuth flows refused for their confirmation code from one network{{ else }}[${ALERT_ENVIRONMENT}] DatasourceError: the OAuth rule "OAuth flows refused for their confirmation code" could not run its query{{ end }}
annotations.summary: {{ if $values }}At least 5 flows from one network were refused in the last 15 minutes because their boxel_confirmation_code was missing, malformed, or sent by a client that may not send one. Someone may be scripting flows that impersonate boxel-cli.{{ else }}Grafana could not run this rule's query. This is the rule's DatasourceError alert, and its Error annotation gives the reason. It shows nothing about OAuth activity. The query reads Loki: check the Loki task and its context canceled and context deadline exceeded errors.{{ end }}
annotations.runbook: The oauth-provider skill (Alerts), and the OAuth Provider dashboard.

rules.title: OAuth consents denied in a burst

model.expr: (sum by (user) (count_over_time({service="realm-server"} |= "boxel:oauth-provider" | json | drop __error__, __error_details__ | line_format `{{ if .log }}{{ regexReplaceAll "^\\[worker [^\\]]+\\]: " .log "" }}{{ else }}{{ regexReplaceAll "^\\[worker [^\\]]+\\]: " __line__ "" }}{{ end }}` | json | channel="boxel:oauth-provider" | event="consent" | outcome="denied" | user!="" [15m])) >= 5) or (sum by (network) (count_over_time({service="realm-server"} |= "boxel:oauth-provider" | json | drop __error__, __error_details__ | line_format `{{ if .log }}{{ regexReplaceAll "^\\[worker [^\\]]+\\]: " .log "" }}{{ else }}{{ regexReplaceAll "^\\[worker [^\\]]+\\]: " __line__ "" }}{{ end }}` | json | channel="boxel:oauth-provider" | event="consent" | outcome="denied" | network!="" [15m])) >= 5)

annotations.title: {{ if $values }}[${ALERT_ENVIRONMENT}] Many OAuth consents denied by one {{ if .Labels.user }}user{{ else }}network{{ end }}{{ else }}[${ALERT_ENVIRONMENT}] DatasourceError: the OAuth rule "OAuth consents denied in a burst" could not run its query{{ end }}
annotations.summary: {{ if $values }}At least 5 consents were denied in the last 15 minutes by one user or from one network. A user who denies again and again is likely being sent consent links they didn't ask for: someone is trying to get them to approve an app.{{ else }}Grafana could not run this rule's query. This is the rule's DatasourceError alert, and its Error annotation gives the reason. It shows nothing about OAuth activity. The query reads Loki: check the Loki task and its context canceled and context deadline exceeded errors.{{ end }}
annotations.runbook: The oauth-provider skill (Alerts), and the OAuth Provider dashboard.

rules.title: boxel-cli codes exchanged from another network

model.expr: sum by (client) (count_over_time({service="realm-server"} |= "boxel:oauth-provider" | json | drop __error__, __error_details__ | line_format `{{ if .log }}{{ regexReplaceAll "^\\[worker [^\\]]+\\]: " .log "" }}{{ else }}{{ regexReplaceAll "^\\[worker [^\\]]+\\]: " __line__ "" }}{{ end }}` | json | channel="boxel:oauth-provider" | event="token-issued" | networkMatch="other" [30m])) >= 3

annotations.title: {{ if $values }}[${ALERT_ENVIRONMENT}] boxel-cli codes exchanged from another network than the one that consented{{ else }}[${ALERT_ENVIRONMENT}] DatasourceError: the OAuth rule "boxel-cli codes exchanged from another network" could not run its query{{ end }}
annotations.summary: {{ if $values }}At least 3 boxel-cli codes in the last 30 minutes were exchanged from a different network than the browser that finished the flow. This is what pasting a loopback address into someone else's session looks like, but the CLI on another machine than the browser (a dev container, a cloud workspace, an SSH port-forward) or a VPN covering only the browser cause it too.{{ else }}Grafana could not run this rule's query. This is the rule's DatasourceError alert, and its Error annotation gives the reason. It shows nothing about OAuth activity. The query reads Loki: check the Loki task and its context canceled and context deadline exceeded errors.{{ end }}
annotations.runbook: The oauth-provider skill (Alerts), and the OAuth Provider dashboard.

model.expr: sum by (client, grant) (count_over_time({service="realm-server"} |= "boxel:oauth-provider" | json | drop __error__, __error_details__ | line_format `{{ if .log }}{{ regexReplaceAll "^\\[worker [^\\]]+\\]: " .log "" }}{{ else }}{{ regexReplaceAll "^\\[worker [^\\]]+\\]: " __line__ "" }}{{ end }}` | json | channel="boxel:oauth-provider" | event="resource-refused" | reason=~"route-not-mapped|insufficient-scope|assume-user" [15m])) >= 20

annotations.title: {{ if $values }}[${ALERT_ENVIRONMENT}] One OAuth connection refused at {{ printf "%.0f" $values.B.Value }} routes{{ else }}[${ALERT_ENVIRONMENT}] DatasourceError: the OAuth rule "One OAuth connection probing routes" could not run its query{{ end }}
annotations.summary: {{ if $values }}One connection (one grant) was refused at least 20 times in the last 15 minutes on routes no scope maps, routes its scopes don't reach, or for asking to act as another user. A working app asks for what it needs; this is an app exploring the API, or a stolen token being tried.{{ else }}Grafana could not run this rule's query. This is the rule's DatasourceError alert, and its Error annotation gives the reason. It shows nothing about OAuth activity. The query reads Loki: check the Loki task and its context canceled and context deadline exceeded errors.{{ end }}

rules.title: One user gaining many OAuth grants

annotations.title: {{ if $values }}[${ALERT_ENVIRONMENT}] One user allowed {{ printf "%.0f" $values.B.Value }} OAuth connections in 30 minutes{{ else }}[${ALERT_ENVIRONMENT}] DatasourceError: the OAuth rule "One user gaining many OAuth grants" could not run its query{{ end }}
annotations.summary: {{ if $values }}One user allowed at least 10 connections in the last 30 minutes. People connect an app once; many in a row is a script driving their signed-in browser, or a user being talked through consent again and again.{{ else }}Grafana could not run this rule's query. This is the rule's DatasourceError alert, and its Error annotation gives the reason. It shows nothing about OAuth activity. The query reads Loki: check the Loki task and its context canceled and context deadline exceeded errors.{{ end }}
